answer: A sybil-resistant economy can charge every identity continuous proof of useful work: each agent must regularly complete small verifiable tasks, checking data or attesting transactions, to keep its standing, like a climber who must keep a ledge underfoot rather than float. A fake identity is cheap to spawn, but keeping a mesa of a thousand fakes alive means paying the work cost for each one, every epoch. That cost scales with the size of the fake army while honest agents earn the work back from real trade, so the ocean of fakes drains the attacker faster than it drains the network.
